newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to propose Algeria peace initiative - diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Italy to propose Algeria peace initiative - diplomat.

text.p: Italy will propose a peace initiative to halt the bloodshed in Algeria's civil war at a meeting next month, a high-ranking diplomat said.

Foreign ministry undersecretary Piero Fassino said in a newspaper interview that the West had underestimated the seriousness of Algeria's civil war and called on the European Union to lead an initiative to stop the violence.

He told the Italian newspaper L'Unita in the interview, published on Monday, that Italy planned to present its peace initiative proposal at a meeting of foreign ministers of Italy, Spain and France on February 3.
"The international community has for too long undervalued the importance of the civil war which has been bloodying Algeria," he was quoted as saying.
"The time has come to make up for lost time, developing an initiative which restores rights, freedom and democracy in the country."
Algeria has been in conflict since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election dominated by the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS). About 60,000 people have died.
"We think that in the next few weeks the EU has to assume a more determined role," said Fassino, one of Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini's top deputies. "We cannot abandon Algeria."

He said Italy, which has been urging the EU to focus on strengthening ties with Mediterranean region countries, was one of only a few countries which had been trying through diplomatic channels to stop the violence in Algeria.
The French government on Monday rebuffed a call for a politicial initiative on Algeria, the former French colony in North Africa.

"Algeria is an independent country and for the moment we think it is the responsiblity of the Algerian people, Algerian leaders, to find solutions to their own problems," Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said.
